items.title: Search Warrant at Mississauga Home Turns Up Six of Nine Coffee Machines Stolen in July Heist
items.summary: Peel Regional Police have arrested two men in connection with the theft of nine high-end commercial coffee machines worth an estimated $85,955 from a Mississauga business, according to a police news release. Police said officers first responded to a break-and-enter at a commercial building on the morning of July 11, and investigators later determined the machines had been listed for sale on an online marketplace. On Nov. 1, police executed a search warrant at a residence near Bloor Street and Fieldgate Drive and recovered six of the nine stolen machines, the release said. Investigators believe the remaining three machines had already been sold online. Police charged Cezary Szuc, 45, and Leslie Ayotte, 57, both of Mississauga, with possession of property obtained by crime. Both men were released on undertakings and are scheduled to appear in court at a later date, according to police. The allegations have not been proven in court.

items.title: Walmart-Sponsored Food Drive Launches as Mississauga Food Bank Visits Hit a 40-Year High
items.summary: Food Banks Mississauga kicked off its 2026 Holiday Drive this week, aiming to raise a record amount to meet surging demand across the city, according to insauga.com. The campaign, sponsored by Walmart Canada, runs from Monday through Jan. 8, 2027, the outlet reported. Food bank officials said one in 10 children in Mississauga relied on Food Banks Mississauga and its network of more than 60 food programs over the past year, citing the agency's latest Annual Impact Report. According to the report, people in Mississauga visited food programs roughly 513,000 times this past year, the highest total in the organization's 40-year history. Insauga.com noted that figure is 444 per cent higher than it was a decade ago, a level the agency now considers the new normal. Officials said the report shows that the city's most vulnerable residents are increasingly turning to food banks for support.

items.title: Living Arts Centre to Host Friday Job Fair Aimed at Newcomers Struggling to Crack the Job Market
items.summary: The Canadian Immigrant Newcomer Fair will bring employers, educational institutions, career advisers and settlement organizations together at the Living Arts Centre on Friday, Nov. 13, according to insauga.com. The free event is meant to help newcomers to Canada and other job seekers make connections and explore employment options, the outlet reported. Insauga.com said a significant share of recent working-age immigrants have reported difficulty finding their first job in Canada, with many citing a lack of local connections or employers not recognizing their foreign work experience. The outlet noted that competition for entry-level positions has also become a concern for younger Canadians born or raised here. According to a Bank of Canada analysis cited by insauga.com, the influx of young newcomers between 2022 and 2024 intensified competition for lower-skilled and entry-level jobs, alongside shifting employer needs and the growing role of artificial intelligence. Organizers say helping newcomers find work that matches their skills remains an important part of their integration into Canadian communities.

items.title: Two Overnight Shutdowns Planned as Hazel McCallion LRT Work Reshuffles Bus Stops Downtown
items.summary: Construction on the Hazel McCallion LRT is forcing temporary platform closures at Mississauga's City Centre Transit Terminal through Nov. 20, according to Mississauga.com. The outlet reported that Platform A closures begin the evening of Nov. 10, shifting affected MiWay routes to temporary boarding locations on nearby Rathburn Road. Mississauga.com said the terminal building itself will stay open during regular hours throughout the work, and that bus schedules are not changing, only the boarding locations. Two full overnight closures of the terminal are planned for Nov. 14 and Nov. 15, according to the report. The outlet noted riders should watch for posted signage directing them to the correct temporary stop during the affected period.

items.title: City's Interactive Map Shows When Crews Will Vacuum Leaves in Your Neighbourhood
items.summary: Mississauga's annual loose leaf vacuum pickup program is underway, and the city has posted an interactive map showing when crews will arrive in each neighbourhood, according to Mississauga.com. The outlet reported that the city revised its leaf vacuum zones from previous years, meaning residents should expect changes to their usual collection windows. Mississauga.com said the program only covers areas with trees older than 35 years and a high concentration of large, mature trees. Collection began in late October and continues until early December, the outlet noted, divided into three colour-coded zones. According to the report, each zone receives two separate rounds of pickup over that period.

items.title: Glenforest Secondary Set to Host Mississauga's Second Youth Hub by Early 2027
items.summary: A second youth hub modeled on a facility that opened in Mississauga three years ago is on track to open at Glenforest Secondary School by late 2026 or early 2027, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that the $6-million Glenforest Youth Hub, located at Fieldgate Drive and Burnhamthorpe Road East, was nearing completion as of late September. Insauga.com said the project follows the success of the $6-million Malton Youth Hub Jonathan Davis Centre, which opened in the city's north end in late 2023. City officials told the outlet the new hub will offer services and programs reflecting the needs of local youth, based on input gathered through focus groups, pop-up engagements and an online survey that drew more than 600 responses, 54 per cent from youth. According to insauga.com, the City of Mississauga and Peel Region are splitting the project's cost, with the two partners finalizing their cost-sharing plan in February 2026.

items.title: Jazz Matinees, Film Screenings and Accessible Concerts Fill Mississauga's Winter Calendar
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is promoting a lineup of live entertainment running through the end of the year, according to the city's own announcement. The city said the schedule includes concerts, movies and family-friendly events held at venues across Mississauga with affordable tickets and free parking. Officials noted that REEL Thursdays, presented in collaboration with TIFF Film Circuit, will run an eight-show series featuring monthly screenings of festival favourites and award-contending films. The city said it is also partnering with Xenia Concerts on family-friendly, accessible concerts designed to embrace neurodiversity and disabilities. For a more intimate setting, the announcement added, Meadowvale Theatre will host matinee performances featuring contemporary jazz music.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Nov. 21 Survey on Downtown Signage, Seeks Artists for Two Cooksville Parks
items.summary: Mississauga is inviting residents to weigh in on a new downtown wayfinding strategy while also seeking artists for two permanent installations in Cooksville parks, according to Mississauga.com. The outlet reported that the city will open an online survey on proposed downtown sign designs starting Nov. 21. Mississauga.com said final designs and an implementation plan are expected to be developed in early 2027, with signs installed starting in April 2027 once funding is secured. In the meantime, the outlet noted, temporary wayfinding signs have been posted on windows, walls and sidewalks downtown. According to the report, the city's Public Art Program is separately looking for professional artists or artist-led teams to take on the two Cooksville projects, with application deadlines of Nov. 12 and Nov. 23.
